draft.title: Graphs of sine and cosine
card: The graph of \(y = \sin x\) is a wave. It starts at \(0\) when \(x = 0^{\circ}\), rises to \(1\) at \(90^{\circ}\), is back to \(0\) at \(180^{\circ}\), falls to \(-1\) at \(270^{\circ}\) and returns to \(0\) at \(360^{\circ}\).

The graph of \(y = \cos x\) has the same wave shape, but it starts at its highest point. It is \(1\) at \(0^{\circ}\), \(0\) at \(90^{\circ}\), \(-1\) at \(180^{\circ}\), \(0\) at \(270^{\circ}\) and \(1\) again at \(360^{\circ}\).
Both waves stay between \(-1\) and \(1\), so their highest value is \(1\) and their lowest is \(-1\).
Both waves repeat every \(360^{\circ}\). So the value at \(x\) is the same as the value at \(x + 360^{\circ}\). For example, \(\sin 400^{\circ} = \sin 40^{\circ}\).

1.alt: The graph of \(y = \sin x\) from \(0^{\circ}\) to \(360^{\circ}\). It starts at \(0\), peaks at \(1\) when \(x = 90^{\circ}\), crosses \(0\) at \(180^{\circ}\), reaches its lowest value of \(-1\) at \(270^{\circ}\) and returns to \(0\) at \(360^{\circ}\).

draft.remember: Sine and cosine are waves between \(-1\) and \(1\) that repeat every \(360^{\circ}\). Sine starts at \(0\), cosine starts at \(1\).

a.why: The wave repeats every \(360^{\circ}\), so \(\sin 450^{\circ} = \sin 90^{\circ} = 1\). The value \(0\) comes from forgetting to subtract \(360^{\circ}\) and treating the angle as a multiple of \(180^{\circ}\).
a.clue: Take away one full turn first.

b.q: Mia sketches \(y = \cos x\) for \(x\) from \(0^{\circ}\) to \(720^{\circ}\). How many times does her graph reach its highest value?
b.why: Cosine starts at its highest value, \(1\), when \(x = 0^{\circ}\). The wave repeats every \(360^{\circ}\), so it is at \(1\) again at \(360^{\circ}\) and \(720^{\circ}\), which is 3 times. Counting only 2 leaves out the starting point.
b.clue: Cosine starts at its highest point. Count that one too.

problems.detail: The why says the wrong answer 0 comes from 'treating the angle as a multiple of 180°', but 450° is not a multiple of 180°. This could confuse students. Say instead that a student might wrongly think sin 450° is 0, as it is at 180° or 360°.

check.summary: Both answers are correct: sin 450° = 1, and cos x reaches 1 three times from 0° to 720°. The only issue is the why for (a), which confusingly says 450° is treated as a multiple of 180° when it is not one.
